items.title: Warhammer Survivors Isn’t Much More Than a Vampire Survivors Reskin, Which Is (Mostly) OK
items.summary: Though it passes up the opportunity to move the genre into new territory, the game is a tasty, if familiar, piece of gaming junk food.
items.content:
Though it passes up the opportunity to move the genre into new territory, the game is a tasty, if familiar, piece of gaming junk food.

Warhammer Survivors often feels like a Vampire Survivors reskin, rather than a standalone game. Auroch Digital When I first heard that developers Auroch Digital and Vampire Survivors creator Luca “Poncle” Galante were working together on Warhammer Survivors, I was thrilled. A studio of Warhammer lore fiends collaborating with a solo dev who birthed a genre seemed like a recipe for success.

But having now played through most of the game’s sci-fi battles and a smattering of fantasy incursions, I think your enjoyment of this game probably hinges entirely on how many modern bullet heaven games you’ve played. If you’re looking for something that meaningfully changes the formula, you won’t find it here.

While Vampire Survivors should be respected and lauded for laying the foundations for an entirely new type of video game, it has been surpassed by newer projects that have fundamentally changed the fledgling bullet heaven genre for the better. Newer games have implemented incredibly robust progression systems , more objective-based gameplay and entirely new camera perspectives .

There’s no problem with Survivors being knocked off the pedestal it built – every developer should learn from their peers, and the oldest games will never be the most polished games (even if they stand the test of time as cult classics).

The issue is that Warhammer Survivors just feels like a massive, reskinned expansion of Poncle’s original game. Despite a striking visual identity and plenty of Warhammer-themed weapons and items, this game never escapes the shadow of Vampire Survivors, which may diminish the enjoyment of genre enthusiasts.

Auroch Digital’s stab at a bullet heaven game isn’t unique, and its thrills wear out sooner than one might expect, but I think that’s mostly OK. It’s full of charming, vibrant Warhammer-themed pixel art, and that feels like what the true appeal of Warhammer Survivors just might be. This is the type of video game junk food that keeps you up until 5 a.m. every once in a while, completely destroying your sleep schedule. It won’t go down as one of the bullet heaven greats, and it doesn’t need to.

Vampire Survivors veterans will have a sense of deja vu from the pixel art-styling and increasing enemy clusters. There’s some extra content and quality-of-life features bolted on here, but you’ll instantly know what you’re getting into.

When players start a run, they’re dropped into iconic locations from a top-down perspective in order to purge the area of ravenous xenos and chaos cultists. The onslaught of enemies grows increasingly fearsome as time wears on, with larger and more dangerous enemies joining the fray. As players dodge and defeat the alien threats, though, they provide experience points and items that exponentially ramp up player power.

Once you start getting your hands on an expanded arsenal of weaponry, it becomes obvious why Auroch Digital was the right choice for this project – it’s a development studio full of folks who obviously love the twin worlds of Warhammer, and that passion can be found in every nook and cranny of Warhammer Survivors.

The game’s visual style is striking, which is something I’ve come to expect from any Auroch Digital game – Warhammer Boltgun has richly detailed pixel art, and the development experience from those boomer shooters has translated extremely well to Warhammer Survivors’ 8-bit arcade trappings. The cost of entry is worth it just to see massive tyranid aliens and chaos space marines rendered in all their retro glory.

And the space marine power fantasy thrives here as players wield some of the most iconic space marine weapons, including gory chainswords, hard-hitting boltguns and face-melting flamers. What’s truly special, though, is how many of the game’s weapons and passive power-ups pay homage to the series’ tabletop roots – I was chuffed to see explosive D6 dice and mini figure glue, which both became a regular part of my screen-clearing builds.

One truly unique feature allows players to collect allies that wield weapons, instead of just building out a one-man arsenal. These allies trail behind the main character, which alters how players may approach hordes of enemies.

Certain characters unlock massive buffs if they continue adding allies to the party, which introduces another way to scale up damage very quickly. This doesn’t change how account-wide progression works, but it’s a new play style that shakes up the Vampire Survivors formula.

items.title: Warhammer Survivors is out now on PC, mobile, and consoles, and so far I’m enjoying it
items.summary: Warhammer Survivors is out now on PC and console, and it brings 40k and Age of Sigmar campaigns to the bullet heaven party.
items.content:
Warhammer Survivors is out today on a whole bunch of different platforms, and I’ve been looking forward to sitting down with this one ever since it was first announced. Well, it’s out now on Android, iOS, PC (Windows), Nintendo Switch 1+2, PS5, and Xbox Series, and it brings a whole mountain of 40k and Age of Sigmar fan service to the table.

Courtesy of access provided by the developers, I’ve spent much of my day today working through both halves of the game, and before I head to bed, it’s time to get whatever thoughts I’ve got out of the ol’ noggin and onto the screen.

As suggested by the title, we’re looking at a reworking of Vampire Survivors but with a Warhammer theme, as developed by Auroch Digital. It officially borrows the formula from poncle’s genre-defining title, and then injects a bunch of Games Workshop flavour into the mix. The result: wholesome, grimdark bullet heaven fun that delivers exactly what you think it’s going to, for better or worse.

I know a bit about Warhammer, certainly enough to appreciate that Auroch Digital has done a good job with the license. And so they should, as this is the studio that gave us the pixel-art 40K boomer shooter, Boltgun. In other words, this is a safe pair of hands, and I don’t think they’ve dropped the ball here.

That’s also not to say that this is a bullet heaven masterpiece because there are areas where it could be enhanced, but I think any limitations I have encountered stem from the game’s adherence to the Vampire Survivors formula, from the feel of the movement through to the progression system, right down to the chonky loading times when opening chests.

It also suffers from a unique problem in the sense that it feels like it’s part of Vampire Survivors because it is so true to the source material, but it also feels a little bit weird to be starting from scratch and going through that early game feeling so underpowered. Perhaps this uneven pacing could have been mitigated by a bit more variety during the earliest hours, where it sometimes feels throttled by its need to follow the well-established progress loop widely used across the whole genre.

There are two halves to Warhammer Survivors, with one focused on the sci-fi world of Warhammer 40,000, while the other is steeped in the lore of Age of Sigmar, its fantasy counterpart.

There is some crossover between the two; for example, Nuln Oil appears as an ability in both. Nuln Oil is a shade that miniature painters will be very familiar with, and it’s a good example of how it doesn’t take long for Warhammer Survivors to find the point of whimsy between the two franchises. It’s not long before dice roll across the battlefield, bouncing between the puddles of Nuln Oil into packs of onrushing hordes against the backdrop of your painting desk.

It’s all very over-the-top and silly, just like Warhammer and just like Vampire Survivors.

There are a few interesting points of difference, such as the companions who follow you around in battle. I liked those, and I like the thematic attacks, too. Although it does definitely feel like a Vampire Survivors game, it’s also a well-implemented theme that feels true to the source material that inspired it.

I generally liked that they split things out into two different sections, but it does have an impact on pacing. Keeping them apart allows the different mechanics and characters to have more room to breathe; however, it forces you to go through that early game loop yet again. If you’re like me and enjoy this part of the bullet heaven experience, you’ll be fine. If you’re among those starting to feel fatigued by the well-worn pathways of survivors-like meta-progress, I daresay you might not be as enthused.

For what it’s worth, at the time of writing, I’ve got just shy of seven hours with the launch version of Warhammer Survivors, and I’ve enjoyed what I’ve seen of it thus far. As a fan of all of its component parts, I’m quite sure that I am going to keep chipping away at this in the background for some time, as there appears to be a lot of content still to unlock. What’s more, with Auroch Digital teasing plans to keep adding fresh champions and more new stuff to the game, there’s every chance that Warhammer Survivors will age quite well.

Still with me? Of course you are! If you want to keep reading about great hand-picked roguelikes, this website is absolutely chock-full of them. Head over to the Guides Page for a concentrated hit of roguish games, organised via sub-genre and platform.

What’s more, there are always going to be new lists for emerging trends as well as fresh titles to highlight. This is because my backlog is embarrassingly long, and so I’m always trying to balance the new games that arrive in my inbox with playing the stuff I already have.

items.title: Mini Review: Warhammer Survivors (PS5) - Absurdly Addictive Crossover Is a Match Made in Bullet Hell
items.content:
Warhammer Survivors is exactly what its name suggests: a Warhammer reskin of Vampire Survivors .

Developed by licensed Warhammer studio Auroch Digital, with Vampire Survivors creator poncle partnering on the project, it's a fantastic, heartfelt adaptation right out of the gate.

Indeed, it's immediately obvious that an awful lot of care has been taken in providing poncle's world-beating gameplay formula with a fresh coat of paint. The Warhammer settings, characters, enemies, and weapons are all there — but the game also relishes in dishing out smaller references to Games Workshop's immensely popular fiction.

In particular, I was left pleasantly surprised by how often Warhammer Survivors pays tribute to the property's tabletop identity. Numerous playable characters, for example, are unlocked by finding miniature figure paints scattered across maps.

Meanwhile, power ups can include rolling damage dice — actual dice — across the battlefield, crushing your foes in the process. You can even drop giant blast radius templates on top of your enemies if you're lucky.

What I'm saying is that Auroch Digital and poncle clearly had loads of fun with this one — it's not just a simple copy and paste job that takes advantage of the Warhammer name.

Oh, and it's basically two games in one. On the main menu, you can pick between Warhammer's dark sci-fi 40,000 setting, and its high fantasy Age of Sigmar setting. Each comes with its own character roster, maps, enemy factions, objectives, upgrades, and everything else, making for a seriously robust package.

Gameplay-wise, the title offers a slight twist on the absurdly addictive Survivors structure. Stages have a 25-minute time limit instead of 30, and I'd say there's a larger emphasis on tactical thinking.

That's because specialised opponents are more prevalent, forcing you to weave your way through the hordes in a more methodical manner. At least, until you rack up so many super-powered upgrades that anything in your path just evaporates anyway.

Yep, that same progression curve that makes Vampire Survivors so insanely moreish is alive and well here, although I do think it takes a little longer to hit those truly chaotic highs because of the aforementioned tweaks.

All in all, Warhammer Survivors perfectly melds Games Workshop's property with poncle's timeless formula, resulting in another exceptional roguelike experience.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass's free Vampire Survivors alternative stole 20 hours of my life in two days
items.summary: Vampire Survivors players have an excellent alternative to play now!
items.content:
I had to tap into the indomitable human spirit whilst playing Warhammer Survivors, as it's as brutal as the universe it's based on.

Last week I had some much-needed time off, and what better way to spend it than with early-access to one of my most-anticipated games of the year. I’ve developed a love-hate relationship with it though.

After the colossal success of Vampire Survivors loads of developers have tried to capitalise off the auto-battler’s success, but few have come close to the OG.

Warhammer Survivors is a different story however. It’s just as good, and I’m not just saying that because I’m a Warhammer fan.

Once installed, my intention was to play for around an hour before sorting out some errands around the house. Five hours later I was still playing.

You’re given the choice between two popular Warhammer settings. The first is Warhammer: Age of Sigmar, which is ideal for fantasy fans, but not really my cup of tea.

My bread and butter is Warhammer 40,000, and experiencing that universe in Vampire Survivors-style was more moreish than I’d ever expected.

The first round starred Ultramarine Malum Caedo, a popular character from the Warhammer 40,000 Boltgun games.

READ NEXT: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2's grimdark goodness is so moreish I'll gladly give Games Workshop more money

A few scrappy Tyranids quickly fell to my chainsaw, with their numbers slowly growing like the satisfaction I felt cleaving through them.

Each level-up grants you a new ability, weapon, or upgrade and I’ve had so much fun unlocking them. I’ve still got plenty left as well, as most are locked behind secret characters.

However it hasn't all been sunshine and rainbows. The reason this game has devoured so much of my free time isn’t just because it’s fun, because it is, it’s also because it infuriates me unlike any other game I’ve played this year.

There’s nothing inherently hard about Warhammer Survivor s. All you do is move around, pick-up upgrades, and try to ensure our attacks are going into the bulk of the enemy’s forces to thin them down.

Like an actual game of Warhammer 40,000 though, luck is a huge factor. At the drop of a hat or the roll of a dice the game can be over in seconds as you didn’t manage to collect the upgrades needed for your build.

I’m all for Survivors- anything, and so the news that Auroch Digital was teaming up with Poncle to bring a Survivors game to the Warhammer universe was music to my ears. And now, having sunk multiple hours into Warhammer Survivors , it’s safe to say I haven’t been disappointed. The marrying of the Warhammer universe and Vampire Survivors works so well that, honestly, it’s a wonder it’s taken this long.

Unsurprisingly, there’s an awful lot of Vampire Survivors DNA in Warhammer Survivors, from the visual effects of opening a treasure chest to the range of upgrades available to you between runs. That’s not to say it’s a copycat; while it’ll obviously be familiar to Vampire Survivors fans, it also manages to feel fresh and unique thanks to its setting within the Warhammer universes. Yes, I do mean universes , plural, because when you start playing, you’re given the choice of Warhammer 40,000 or Age of Sigmar.

Technically, then, you’re getting two games in one with Warhammer Survivors, with each universe offering distinct environments, different characters and separate upgrades. Sure, some of the weapons and attacks are the same across both universes, but it’s easily forgiven, given the sheer amount of content available here.

In Warhammer 40,000 you’ll initially play as a Space Marine, although as you progress through the game you’ll unlock more characters, all with their own unique starting abilities. The same is true of Age of Sigmar, where you’ll start as Stormcast Neave Blacktalon. Like with any Survivors-like, you’ll gather experience tokens as you defeat enemies, levelling up each time your experience bar is full. Every level up will allow you to choose a new passive or active ability, or upgrade an existing one. Survive long enough, and you’ll be able to become a formidable force to be reckoned with. But that’s a big if : Warhammer Survivors doesn’t go easy on you, and surviving the early stages is going to test your mettle.

It’s safe to say that Warhammer Survivors is much more difficult than Vampire Survivors. The skills you unlock are based on weapons and abilities from the wider Warhammer universe, so they’re generally less fantastical than those found in Vampire Survivors. It means your starting ability might be a forward-firing weapon, or a small area of effect attack that does minimal damage. Of course, they can all be levelled up as you gain experience, becoming more powerful over time. But it feels much harder to become as formidable as you can in other Survivors-like experiences – at least not until you’ve grinded enough to earn multiple permanent upgrades.

You’ll be able to spend coins earned during a run to level up things like your base HP, attack power, how long attacks last, the size of attacks and a whole lot more, with those upgrades applying to every run you have. You will have unique progress in both Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar, though, giving you good reason to spend time in both. It at least means that no run ever feels like a complete waste of time; even if you succumb to enemies after a matter of minutes, you’ll have earned some progress towards a new permanent upgrade.

With both Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar having their own characters to unlock, environments to explore and goals to work towards, there are dozens of hours of gameplay in each experience. It makes Warhammer Survivors a seriously attractive prospect to any fan of Survivors-like games, and you don’t need to know anything about Warhammer to enjoy it (although it’ll undoubtedly help). Given its asking price of around £6.49/$7.99, it’s an absolute steal.

This review of Warhammer Survivors is based on the PS5 version of the game, with a code provided by the publisher. It’s available on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch, Switch 2 and PC.

items.title: Despite promising a heady mix of Vampire Survivors and Warhammer fan-service, Warhammer Survivors is somehow less than the sum of its parts
items.summary: But then, maybe the stress of the early game even makes Warhammer Survivors' eventual catharsis even better...
items.content:
Image credit: Eurogamer Feature by Dom Peppiatt Deputy Editorial Director Published on Nov. 10, 2026, 2:06 p.m. 14 comments Follow Warhammer Survivors Prioritise us on Google You know my favourite thing about Vampire Survivors ? The slow build of strength, the swelling power fantasy, the edging . Developer Poncle has proved itself incredibly adept at goading players into ever more ludicrous setups, demonstrating that with some patience, a canny eye for build-crafting, and some very rudimentary knowledge of your surroundings, even an old man armed with garlic can be an extinction level event for the amassing undead. Warhammer Survivors sadly never reaches those heights.

Created by Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 studio Auroch Digital, Warhammer Survivors is - as its name suggests - an officially-licensed attempt to transplant developer Poncle's winning Vampire Survivors' formula to the Warhammer universe. Cue 40+ characters ripped from Warhammer lore getting the action-roguelike treatment, crossbows instead of clock lancets, rocket launchers instead of fire wands, bomb Squids instead of skeletons… you get the idea.

But this fusion doesn't really work. While Vampire Survivors was always a bit of an uphill battle from the start, it still hooked you with a thread that pulled you forward, tempting you with power-ups and other intriguing toys to play with en route. If hour one was a slog, hour five sparked curiosity, and hour 10 was a romp. In Warhammer Survivors, however, hour 10 feels like just as much of a slog as hour one. And even though Warhammer Survivors offers two alternate universes - the grimdark future of 40K and the old-school fantasy of Age of Sigmar, each a full game in its own right - this does little to alleviate the grind.

It's all so slow. Characters move slowly, upgrades come slowly, unlocking the mode that makes things move a bit faster comes slowly. Every inch feels like a mile, and the moreish power creep - tantalisingly propulsive in Vampire Survivors - is out of reach for so long per run here, it's discouraging. That's not to say there isn't any resolution to all the tension. Every now and then, you'll roll the right dice, appease the right gods, make the right moves. Your miniature pixel heroes will overcome the odds, and burn through the writhing mass of Orks, Skaven, Tyranids, Nurgle, or whatever other bastards are trying to get you down today.

The Survivors genre - sometimes known as 'bullet heaven' now - lives and dies on the strength of the over-powered nonsense that emerges as all your weapons and evolutions start to harmonise with each other in brutal synchronicity. Warhammer Survivors seems reluctant to let you get to this level, though. Even 30 hours in (!), some runs will end before they ever really get started - no matter how many skips, rerolls, or other chance-altering upgrades you've committed to your save file.

And because this is really two games glued into one, you have to do all the requisite grinding and levelling on both sides. With massive maps and impossibly slow character movement (especially on some of the bulkier characters), collecting all the items per location is more of a chore than it is fun. This wouldn't be so bad if these items were just curios, but in most cases they're pretty significant quality-of-life enhancers. Why are you hiding them from me, Auroch!?

It's almost impressive how Warhammer Survivors manages to feel like a step back from Poncle's original in many ways: yes, there's more content, but there appears to be a lack of understanding of why this genre immediately took off and spawned a myriad of imitators. The very worst weapons are the only ones available at the beginning, so unlocking new characters and armaments is necessary rather than a fun bonus. Lore is paper thin - in Vampire Survivors, we had a blank canvas and the lack of lore didn't really matter, but Warhammer is steeped in its own mythos, so relegating it to merely set dressing feels remiss. Some of the synergies between items and their evolutions don't really make sense. The maps are awkward and fussy to navigate. The locked requirements to take on stage-end bosses are even more cryptic than in Vampire Survivors. In almost all the ways that matter when it comes to fun , Warhammer Survivors pales in comparison to its forebear. This wouldn't be so egregious if the game wasn't trying to emulate it quite so completely, but it is - and as such, all the actually decent design choices hidden behind layers of frustration are marred.

As a Warhammer and Survivors fan, I've found myself floating back to the game, even if - sometimes - my eyes roll back into my head within minutes of my first run. But it's not a complete disaster: on those occasions where the stars do align, Warhammer Survivors finds its way to a power fantasy worthy of both franchises. You'll grab a Flamer early doors, then pick up the passive Glue to reduce incoming damage. You'll gain the Heavy Flamer, the Boltgun, and the projectile-multiplying Dice Cube, eventually unlocking the Heavy Bolter - slicing through enemies and all but melting the face off that pesky Prophet of Gork.

I just wish there wasn't so much friction in actually getting to that point. I imagine Warhammer Survivors is the sort of game I'll keep on my harddrive (and on multiple devices; it costs a fiver and it's on Game Pass) for a while. If you can endure the teething pains and engage with the wobblier systems, there's the usual Survivors payoff waiting for you as the screen fills with pixelated blood and countless helpless enemies fall to your blades. Maybe the stress of the early game even makes this catharsis even better. So even with its qualms, Warhammer Survivors is still an enjoyable, lo-fi stress reliever to snack on in between other, meatier games.

items.title: Warhammer Survivors Out Now on XBOX Game Pass! Defeat the Gloomspite Gitz With These Tips
items.summary: Warhammer Survivors is out now on XBOX Series X|S and XBOX Game Pass! Take a closer look at the Gloomsite Gitz enemy faction.
items.content:
If this is your first time hearing about Warhammer Survivors , buckle in for addictive bullet-heaven survivor gameplay set across the battlefields of the 41st Millennium and the Mortal Realms. You might know us, Auroch Digital, from our other Warhammer game, Warhammer 40,000 Boltgun . We’ve teamed up with poncle and Warhammer to create an officially licensed Warhammer Survivors .

Following the green theme of our previous entry , we’ve prepared a primer for you to take on the fungus-festooned Gloomspite Gitz!

The Gloomspite Gitz are a rabble of different cave-dwelling grots that worship the ‘Bad Moon’, a deity they believe will bring about the Everdank, an era of perpetual twilight. This calamitous cohort of crazed Gitz includes several enemy types, each with their own unique attacks and movement patterns you’ll need to learn to have any chance of survival!

Moonclan Stabbas are the foot soldiers of the Gloomspite Gitz, swarming the battlefield in tremendous numbers, stabbing wildly at everything in their path. Moonclan Stabbas try to overwhelm with sheer number of bodies and sharp, pointy objects – and while they may not be the scariest, look out for the company they keep…

…And the stampeding forces of the Squigalanche!

Squig Hoppers are grots that have bravely decided to mount feral Squigs and have somehow survived the process. These enemies bounce across the battlefield in unpredictable movements due to the nature of their wild mounts, and their attack damage will be bolstered by any nearby Loonboss on Giant Cave Squig who – you guessed it – also moves unpredictably!

Boinggrot Bounders , on the other hand, are veteran Squig-riders who have survived at least one battle (the life expectancy of a grot is low). For their prowess, they’ve been rewarded with lances, charging with precision toward the player.

Stampeding at the head of this Squigalanche are the wild and gargantuan Mangler Squigs. These two boisterous balls of fury are so ravenous they’ve been chained together. The beasts rampage across the screen, pulled taut by the chain that binds them together. Watch out for both the teeth of Mangler Squig and the chain as each can damage the player. Mangler Squigs always come in pairs, but when one dies, the remaining giant Squig becomes frenzied – deadlier than ever before!

If you can survive the pointy blades of the Gitz and the sharp teeth of the Squigs, then you may encounter an even greater threat… Troggoths!

Rockgut Troggoths lumber toward the player, and while they may be slow, they’re tough and have regeneration properties, making them tricky to bring down. Our recommendation? Get yourself a pair of Maleneth’s Poisoned Daggers and whittle them down from afar.

Should you survive all that, then we’ve got news for you: it doesn’t get better!

Trugg the Troggoth King is the mightiest of all troggoths, a towering mass of strength with an ill temper. He carries an arcane keystone of ancient design on his back which unleashes unpredictable bursts of elemental magic…

If you somehow manage to be strong enough to face this foe, he’ll begin the fight by swiping at you with his humungous Ironshell Club, which creates wide, telegraphed impact zones. If you’re hit, you’ll be sent flying. Trugg. You’ll also have to contend with that keystone of his, avoiding wild barrages of elemental projectiles. Getting hit by one of these stray projectiles will inflict your Survivor with negative status effects such as burning, poisoning, or bleeding.

As an Extremis-level threat, not just anyone, or any weapon, will be able to take down the Troggoth King. You’ll have to discover what his weakness is or face certain death!

The phenomenon of Vampire Survivors has been unreal, with this small $5 game becoming one of the most popular video games in history. It spawned its own genre, along with getting huge collaborations with incredible franchises like Castlevania and Contra. Now, developer Poncle is branching out, working with other developers to make Survivors games of their own. We have seen other games in this genre already, but none that have encompassed Vampire Survivors so closely. However, that’s exactly what Warhammer Survivors does, and it was surprisingly different from what I expected.

Don’t get me wrong, Warhammer Survivors is extremely similar to Vampire Survivors, and anyone who loves the latter will love the former. At the same time, it stands on its own two feet, adding enough differences to justify it being its own game rather than just DLC for Vampire Survivors. Ultimately, it was hard not to fall in love with the game, and I could not keep myself away once I started playing.

The gameplay is extraordinarily similar to Vampire Survivors, so I was able to pick up and start playing without any learning curve to worry about. We run across the map, level up, collect and upgrade new weapons and passive items, and try to survive as long as we can against the horde of enemies coming at us. As time goes on, the quantity grows, getting to a point where almost the entire screen is filled up with enemies we need to kill. It’s chaotic and exciting, simple and addictive, and it just hits all the right marks to keep me wanting to come back for more and more.

It’s almost completely identical to Vampire Survivors in this sense, but it still never gets old. However, this is where the differences start to come into play and really push its own identity as a survivors game for Warhammer fans.

The entire game is themed around different Warhammer universes. It’s obvious as soon as you open the game and have the choice between playing in the Warhammer 40,000 or Age of Sigmar universes. In a sense, it’s similar to the mini campaigns from the Vampire Survivors DLC, but expands on it greatly. Each universe has its own stages, weapons, characters, enemies, and unlockables that relate directly to its lore. We even see some familiar characters, which made me a little giddy since I started playing this right after finishing Boltgun 2.

It was cool seeing all the different weapons and how they work. We can get something as simple as the Boltgun or Chainsword, or we could get claws that slash right in front of us or a weapon that can make missiles drop down from the sky. Each weapon felt different enough from the others to justify having them all here, and the evolution of each of them was exciting to see. My favorite was the Boltgun’s evolution, since we spray bullets in front of us and can mow down hundreds of enemies around us with ease. However, I did enjoy the Shotgun getting homing bullets and the Shield of Faith turning into a giant flaming circle that can heal us whenever it kills an enemy. Combine it with the right passes, and it can be huge, deadly, and constantly healing us.

Some weapons we will get aren’t compatible with our selected character either (I can’t see a dog being able to shoot guns), and that’s where Followers come in. Followers are basically extra characters that follow us around the map, like we have our own posse of slayers. It’s a cool new idea, but I wasn’t a fan of it. The weapons the followers wield come from them, which makes them come from a different location entirely. It was a little jarring as I was planning for my own character, but trying to direct where the Boltgun would shoot from a character following me got a little more difficult.

I actually found Warhammer Survivors’ gameplay a little more difficult as well. It wasn’t impossible, but I died way more often than I expected. It’s possible I just thought of myself as a veteran because of all the time I spent playing Vampire Survivors, but it was clear that if I was going to succeed, I was going to have to try much harder. I learned which weapons worked the most, I figured out their synergies, and when the huge Extremis bosses appeared at the end of some of the levels, I was ready. Sort of. These new bosses do require a specific evolved weapon to actually hurt them, but defeating them can unlock new content.

Speaking of which, there’s a bunch of new content that’s in both campaigns, and it will take some time to get them. Even at the 20-hour mark, I had only completed about 51% of the Warhammer 40,000 campaign, and there was definitely a lot more I knew I could do. We can look through the Objectives tab to see what we can unlock and how, and I felt like there was always something I could work towards. Even 50 hours in, I still felt like I had a goal to achieve that I felt motivated for. And even with the difficulty spike, it never felt old.

As for playing Warhammer Survivors on the Steam Deck, it feels like a dream come true. Hell, it sometimes feels even better than Vampire Survivors, which I found a little crazy.

The game sticks to 90 FPS almost the entire time, only starting to show cracks when the entire screen is blowing up with effects and enemies. Even still, it doesn’t drop from 90, only causing some stutters here and there. These may be unavoidable, but it never stopped the game from feeling smooth enough to enjoy. And the battery always stayed below 14W, averaging around 8-9W for 95% of the game. Even with the jumps in battery and some stuttering towards later parts of stages, it never stopped the flow enough to dissuade from playing.

items.title: Warhammer Survivors Isn’t Good Enough to Be a Vampire Survivors Replacement
items.summary: Warhammer Survivors shows that good video game clones are a sincere form of flattery
items.content:
By Tomas Franzese Published Nov 10, 2026, 5:00 AM EST Tomas Franzese is the Weekend News Editor at Polygon, following and reporting on the latest goings-on in the gaming and entertainment spaces. During the week, you can find him working on Remastered , his newsletter about video game history and retro gaming, or contributing to GameSpot and other publications. Previously, Tomas was the Gaming Segment Lead at XDA and a Staff Writer at Digital Trends . Impressions Good clones are the sincerest form of flattery

Warhammer Survivors screenshot Image: Auroch Digital Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Sign in to your Polygon.com account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Vampire Survivors and its plethora of clones are always more fun in hour ten than hour one. The passive nature of the auto-attack gameplay means this style of experience lives or dies by how fun and visually over-the-top the action can get once you upgrade your character, gain access to more weapons, and manage to survive long enough to level up or evolve your weapons.

I did eventually hit that point of satisfaction with Warhammer Survivors , which was developed by Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 studio Auroch Digital with help from Vampire Survivors creator Poncle. When I got to the point where I could rip and tear through enemies with a Typhoon Crossbow as followers with upgraded weapons of their own fired at enemies around it, the game offered spectacle worthy of the Warhammer and Survivors names. But getting there doesn’t feel quite as good as its inspiration.

Warhammer Survivors doesn’t contain any sort of important lore to speak of; it’s more of a hodgepodge of various recognizable Warhammer characters (like Boltgun’s Malum Caedo) fighting against waves of unrelenting creatures from both eras of the franchise. Warhammer Survivors is essentially two games in one, with one half based on the sci-fi Warhammer 40,000 and the other on the more fantasy-like Warhammer: Age of Sigmar .

Each half of Warhammer Survivors has unique characters, weapons, enhancements, and objectives to unlock, but the core gameplay loop of each is the same. As a player, all you have to do is walk around levels as your character automatically attacks. Enemies drop experience when they die most of the time, and you collect that to level up and upgrade all of the weapons that you have equipped. Considering Poncle was directly involved with this game, it’s not surprising that Warhammer Survivors does not do much to hide its inspiration or reinvent the formula.

The most unique gimmick here is a follower feature, which solves for the fact that Warhammer Survivors’ characters are connected to factions that only let them use specific weapons. Rather than one character wielding every weapon and upgrading at once, sometimes you can save or summon another character that uses a different weapon to fight alongside you. This feels fitting for the large-scale battles Warhammer is known for. Yet in practice, all it really does is add an additional layer to a choice you were already going to make regardless.

Warhammer Survivors screenshot Image: Auroch Digital It shouldn’t be too surprising that what you’re getting with this game is Vampire Survivors with a Warhammer coat of paint, even if it does go a bit deeper than Vampire Survivors’ typical crossover DLC . Vampire Survivors is a great game, and Warhammer Survivors is a good one too. That said, I won’t herald Warhammer Survivors as some amazing replacement for that indie classic, because there are some things it doesn’t do quite as well as the original.

Survivors games are all about snowballing power, building up to a chaotic storm of attacks. In Vampire Survivors , almost every weapon has auto aim and will hit something in range when used. But that’s not the case for certain early-game weapons in Warhammer Survivors that shoot the direction the player is facing, like the Boltgun. Those simply don’t mesh well with the auto-attacking gameplay.

The lack of auto-aim on these weapons meant that, as I moved to avoid enemies, I would shoot away from the horde, toward nothing. Eventually, I was able to unlock better weapons that would actually hit the enemies approaching me, but the fact that the earliest weapons are some of the worst means it takes a bit too long to find the fun.

Warhammer Survivors screenshot Image: Auroch Digital By hour 10 with Vampire Survivors , I had found the characters and weapons I enjoyed using the most. They tended to be the ones that would allow me to exponentially increase in power most smoothly and actually felt like I could survive 20+ minutes and 40+ levels into a single run. From that point onwards, Warhammer Survivors is as good as Vampire Survivors or any other game of its ilk. It’s just not quite as instantly captivating and rewarding.

Diehard Warhammer fans who haven’t played Vampire Survivors or any of the games it inspired will have a fantastic time with this, but there’s not much reason to abandon the original Vampire Survivors for this official clone. Warhammer Survivors certainly won’t usurp its direct inspiration as my go-to game of this style because it forgets to emulate some of what made Vampire Survivors near-perfect. Still, it confidently delivers exactly what the title promises.

items.title: Dungeon Crawler Carl Meets Vampire Survivors In 9/10 100-Hour Free RPG
items.summary: This free RPG has 100+ hours of content.
items.content:
Art from Realm of the Mad God showcasing various enemies. Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Tom Wilson Published Nov 8, 2026, 12:00 AM EST Tom Wilson is a Gaming Features Writer at Screen Rant. Over the past five years, Tom has worked as the Editor-in-Chief at The Game Crater, as a Staff Writer for GamingIntel, a List Writer at TheGamer, and, of course, as a Senior Writer at ScreenRant. Tom has experience writing reviews, guides, news, and features, and has been responsible for teams of writers, training them and editing their work. Tom graduated with a Masters in Multimedia Journalism, and has since gone on to build up his portfolio of games journalism work. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap The sheer number of games like Vampire Survivors releasing today is utterly staggering. Its overwhelming visuals, endless barrage of upgrades, and deceptively complex gameplay are understandably enticing, further bolstered by the low price point and spec requirements. It is no wonder that Vampire Survivors and its abundance of pretenders have garnered such critical and commercial acclaim, especially in an era dominated by elevator-pitch concepts and a desire to move away from the relentless onslaught of live service fluff.

If the leagues of other games like Vampire Survivors have not yet proved sufficient, then there is another title worth trying. This massive, 100+ hour RPG takes a lot of the very best aspects of Vampire Survivors , sprinkles a healthy dash of Dungeon Crawler Carl -esque elements, and adds a core multiplayer component to craft a compelling experience that you can play completely for free. The best part is that it's a relatively old title, meaning it's had years of updates, improvements, and new features, all of which are available for you to enjoy right now.

The player fighting a boss in Realm of the Mad God. With even Warhammer getting a Survivors -like game , it feels as if every demographic has been catered to. This includes, of course, the Dungeon Crawler Carl fans, those looking for an experience closer to an RPG, or at least one involving dungeon delving and deadly boss battles. Fortunately, the long-running MMO (which predates the wonderful Vampire Survivors ), Realm of the Mad God , fits this bill perfectly, offering a chaotic, visually overwhelming, dungeon-based, RPG experience with bullet hell, Survivors -esque gameplay.

Released back in 2012, Realm of the Mad God has proven to be one of the most compelling MMOs on the market; its simplistic visuals and compelling core premise, alongside its huge focus on co-operative play and community, have helped keep its player counts consistently high, as has the steady stream of meaningful updates. Easily ranking among the greatest MMOs ever made , Realm of the Mad God , much like Vampire Survivors , understands how to hook the player and keep them coming back.

Its combination of a roguelike and MMO makes for an utterly unique experience unlike any other. It features permadeath, but it doesn't feel as punishing as one would expect from an MMO; the abundance of loot is ever tantalizing, as are the numerous classes you can choose from, the focus on group activities, and every high-stakes encounter that sees the screen awash with pixelated projectiles cascading wildly. Ostensibly, Realm of the Mad God dared to dream of an MMO Vampire Survivors over a decade before it came out.

The player in a shop in Realm of the Mad God. Being an MMO that has been around for nearly 15 years, Realm of the Mad God features hundreds of hours of content for players to get stuck into. You can also play it for free fairly reliably; its vast array of microtransactions typically skews toward the realm of cosmetics and convenience. Of course, that doesn't mean you won't encounter some level of grind or frustration, but you're bound to get a rather substantial amount of Vampire Survivors -esque fun out of it long before you hit that point.

Realm of the Mad God is currently only available on PC. You can download it via its official Steam store page .

One has to enjoy MMOs, however, in order to truly get the most out of Realm of the Mad God . While it is certainly playable solo, engaging with its guilds or playing with friends is ultimately the main way of enjoying it. Should you engage with its community and co-operative gameplay, you'll have a great time and find yourself with dozens, if not hundreds, of hours of fun. If you've been looking for a Vampire Survivors -like with a dash of Dungeon Crawler Carl sprinkled in, then you should absolutely give Realm of the Mad God a try.

Hi everyone, we have a lot happening around new games and Vampire Survivors, so here's a gigantic news post! 🟣- Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton 🔴- Vampire Survivors 1.15 🔴- Legacy of the Bloodmoon teasers 🔴- Legacy of the Moonspell info 🔴- Workshop Support for Vampire Survivors 🔴- ARG and Character Community Challenge winners 🔴- Vampire Survivors Comics 🔵- Vampire Crawlers updates 🟢- PoncleUp

🟣 Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton

A few days back we announced Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton in collaboration with Shueisha Games! Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton is a game like Vampire Survivors, but with a twist: you'll be able to play an 8-player survivors royale PvPvE mode! Some in-game names and terminology are still in development and may be subject to change. While every player plays in their own world, you accumulate points by defeating curses and sorcerers, and with every 100 points accumulated you get to choose a Rule Change that can affect everyone's game. Some Rule Changes are INSANE, but for now we'll just reveal the simple ones you can see in the trailer (silence, slow, steal points...). But Rule Changes aren't the only way to interact with other players. Introducing a world first, mind blowing, unbelievable game mechanic: PRESS A BUTTON. While you move your auto-attacking character, your special attack also builds up. By PRESSING A BUTTON when the special attack is ready, you get to unleash your character's Special Attack, or, if that character can, a DOMAIN EXPANSION! Other players can be caught in the effect of your Domain or Special Attack, so you have to keep an eye on other players' position and special-bar status. A very important aspect of the 8-players mode is the Live Match Status Feed (working name). This big chunk of UI on the left side of the screen constantly updates in real time, acting not only as a scoreboard, but also sending out warnings and all kind of information about what the other players are up to. At the end of the 15 minutes battle royale, the 2 players with the most points will face one another in a 19 seconds duel. Despite the online focus, Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton is a game you can also play alone, in a mission-based mode, just like Vampire Survivors. If you don't ever want to go online, you'll still be able to play the 8-players battle royale mode against bots. This is a game you buy once and can play anytime. We'll keep supporting the game after launch, with our usual style of content updates. So forget about gatcha elements or a forever-evolving PvP meta keeping your time and wallet hostages: our focus here are fun and affordability. Apologies if you had enough of this wall of text, but I kepty mouth shut for almost two years and I haven't even got to the technical bits yet! Yes, the game runs on the Vampire Survivors - First Survivaton framework, so you can expect that same familiar experience playing it, but we had to do several unique tweaks for Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble Survivaton. Other than the obvious, completely new networking for the gameplay and Live Match Status Feed, we have doubled the resolution at which the game runs. That allowed us to completely rebuild the whole VFX pipeline so that we could re-create the distinctive look of Curse Energy and the changes the whole stage depending on activated Domain Expansions or Special Attacks. Another reason to double the resolution was to properly display the UI (that has been completely reworked at framework level) and the Live Match Status Feed, that is capable of also streaming gameplay snippets from other online players. You'll see a lot of other tweaks, like the fact that characters look different if they are seen from the left or from the right, a "default attack" per character that triggers without any weapon, or walls that are actually solid to name a few. Then there are other changes that won't be noticeable until you get to play the game. For example, while we are going by the same content-unlock-philosophy as Vampire Survivors, we are completely reworking the progression in the various game modes and also per-character, so that every game mode will feel fresh even to VS veterans. That's all for now, I hope you have enjoyed the trailer; my favourite part was that bit were Gojo takes a walk.

🔴 Vampire Survivors 1.15 available on all platforms

Please join the Discord or keep an eye on the Updates version of the wiki if you're interested in knowing the fixes in each update (I won't spam Steam News every week for small tweaks).

🔴 Bloodmoon character tease

Legacy of the Bloodmoon is almost complete and we will be able to start testing and submissions soon! That means we'll have an actual release date soon too. In the meantime, here's a Character Spotlight video about Malice Bloodmoon:

🔴 ARG and Community Character Competition winners

Congratulations to the trio of winners of the Lucca Comics ARG: Jenoss, Miryel, Siming, and GIU_LLS (:poemg:?), and to DissonantSynth for winning the Community Challenge! We're finally getting into the design stage of the characters, with a first implementation that will soon be shared with the winners, behind the scenes, to start iterating together on gameplay mechanics. You can expect a few surprises and little extras about them when they'll make their appearance in the game! Baron Husker and Sefi Rotto (:poemg:?) will come alive in a later update, v1.17

🔴 First steps for Steam Workshop support

Instead of waiting the conclusion of the current cycles of updates for Vampire Survivors as originally planned, we will develop modding support over time, one feature at a time. Feature 1 will be about adding CUSTOM (private/local) and WORKSHOP (public/Steam Workshop) characters! Please join the Discord or use the public-beta forum if you're interested in trying out custom characters before they go live on the main branch, in a future update (currently aiming for v1.17)

🔴 Vampire Survivors Comics

Vampire Survivor is getting comics! We've been working with Titan Comics on a 4-issue series, written by David Hazan and illustrated by Jimm Kucaj, with the first issue coming out this September, available in 3 cover variants. Some familiar Vampire Survivors will go through Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, Dairy Plant, and a few other places, and there might even be some lore in there. Issue #1 is available to pre-order from your local comic shop or from Forbidden Planet if you're in the UK / EU. You can find out more about the comics on the Titan Comics website.

🔵 Vampire Crawlers: first QOL update

Our first update to Vampire Crawlers add an Endless mode and several QOL improvements! You can find more details, the strategy behind future updates, and some content spoilers in the Steam News here.

🟢 Countup to the next announcement

Look, we're doing a lot of stuff across several small teams. I'm always happy to write the Steam News but I cannot bombard your feed with everything we're doing. Also took me something like 3 weeks to set this all up. So if you'd like to hear about what we're doing a bit more often, then please visit poncleup.com to see a recap or subscribe to our newsletter. It's a countup instead of a countdown because, as you might have noticed, we're release-date-averse and have no idea ourselves when we'll drop something new 🤷‍♂️ Just know that the newsletters are written by the marketing team :vsskull: Alright, I'm done with work, time to go back having fun on my secret project. Thank you everyone, I'll leave you in the self-proclaimed capable hands of the marketing team! - Luca

Hi everyone! As anticipated several months ago, we’ve been working on several core systems of VS to be able to keep making more content, increase stability, and improve performance. It’s been a while so we have quite a few things to cover today: - a new expansion for VS - a new update - a new poncle team in Japan - the very sensible reason why Vampire Survivors has a sub-title now 🤷‍♂️

Vampire Survivors Update 1.15 (The Wet One) is out now on Steam!

You can find all details about 1.15 below, now here’s a stupid summer trailer about it:

Major QOL improvements

  • Multiple Save Slots (about time!)
  • Character Setup panel for skins, egg selection, etc…
  • Content filters in Character Selection and Unlocks menu
  • Stability improvements for late game and low-end platforms
  • Reduced loading times (more noticeable on other platforms than PC)

New content

  • 1 New Stage: The Lycaeum
  • 2 New Characters
  • either 2 or 10 new weapons 🤷‍♂️
  • 3 New Darkanas
  • 1 New Music Track
  • 3 new Relics, of which 1 Secret rather than Unlockable

Other tweaks and features

  • "Random LevelUp" can now be toggled during a run if it is already unlocked on the Stage menu
  • Added option to Unbanish a weapon when picking it up from the stage
  • Buffed a few weapons like Magi-Stone and Mille Bolle Blu
  • Rendering fixes for a few weapons, including birds, Prismatic Missile, Runetracer…
Patch 1.15 will be released on all other platforms a bit later, by the end of the month, due to platform-specific optimizations and differences in save slots management. On the bright side, we will also be releasing a Nintendo Switch 2 version, with better performance and mouse support!

Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is coming Summer 2026

https://store.steampowered.com/app/4781330/Vampire_Survivors_Legacy_of_the_Bloodmoon/ Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is our “accidental” next expansion and the evil twin to Legacy of the Moonspell. The original plan was just to make a little content update to Legacy of the Moonspell. Since it’s the first and smallest VS expansion, it felt right to try to balance its value a little. Needless to say, ideas started to flow and everything spiraled into a much bigger project. I’m not sure I’ll ever learn at this stage. In the end, Legacy of the Moonspell will be getting its content buff (7 new unlocks) and Legacy of the Bloodmoon will live a life of its own. This expansion pack follows Clan Bloodmoon as they retrace the pilgrimage of Saint Baal’Thasar, in search of a paradise lit by (you guessed it) a bright red moon. There is also an ancient manor that may or may not hide the secret of immortality. Legacy of the Bloodmoon will contain:
  • 12 new villains friendly characters
  • 16+ new weapons and evolutions, including a FireBall
  • 8 savage new music tracks
  • 1 new adventure
  • 1 new very large stage
  • Interesting bits and bobs I won’t spoil at this time
But there’s more. Legacy of the Bloodmoon will cost approximately 1 money (0.99 USD), and Legacy of the Moonspell will receive a price cut and also be priced 1 money :) You can find all details about Legacy of the Bloodmoon below, now here’s a villainous trailer about it:

Vampire Survivors - First Survivaton

Among the many projects we’re working on (approximately 15 projects, not 15 games, please don’t panic) there is also a lineup of Survivaton games. It’s definitely a meaningful word that means “survive a ton” and nothing else. These are games like Vampire Survivors, developed internally at poncle, tied to IPs that might need unique game mechanics, a different graphic style, or are so expansive that ultimately deserve their own standalone game (compared to making a DLC for VS). I’d love to make examples, but I’d have to spoil way too much. Being developed internally, we’ll be able to guarantee affordability and worthwhile titles. Since a good 90% of global VS players aren’t reached by the Steam news (or are not interested in gaming news in general), the best way to also let them know that the Survivatons are tied directly to VS is to also call VS a Survivaton, hence the new sub-title. Please note there’s a dash before First Survivaton instead of a semi-colon, because DLCs exist... The next time I name a game I’ll remember to not use something as generic as “Monster Hunter” as inspiration please know I love Monster Hunter 💌

poncle Japan

We can finally say we are building poncle Japan! It will be poncle, but in Japan. The new studio is headed by Sawaki Takeyasu, known for his work on Devil May Cry, Ōkami, and El Shaddai: Ascension of the Metatron. Having a studio in Japan will simplify and speed up the work we do with all our Japanese partners, and also bring new opportunities for collabs. It’s too soon to say what the team will be working on; we are planning to fully open the studio by the end of 2026. Now it's time for all the FAQs and info blocks, thanks for reading and waiting patiently for this update! - Luca

Legacy of the Bloodmoon FAQs

When does it release? Summer 2026. What do you define as summer? Not winter. How much does it cost? Around £0.95, with regional pricing varying by platform and country. Why will Legacy of the Moonspell’s price change too? It felt right to adjust the price so that it’s more balanced compared to the amount of content of the other expansions. Please note that some stores have minimum prices in certain countries. In some places, Moonspell was already too cheap to make it cheaper. What about Tides of the Foscari then? Please at least wait for Moonspell and Bloodmoon before asking for more, we know we know 😭 Will Moonspell get new content too? Yes, 7 new unlocks for a few more weapons and characters. Is Vampire Survivors still getting free updates? Yes of course, there’s still plenty on the roadmap.

Update 1.15 Full spoilers

♫ Murder on the Seafloor Composed and arranged by Filippo Vicarelli.

Quick content guide:

  • Collect a total of 50 Vacuums to unlock The Lycaeum stage
  • Find the Penshin Fatcha in The Lycaeum and see all its evolutions to unlock it permanently
  • Survive 20 minutes in The Lycaeum to unlock Para Kooleo
  • Trigger a Lavatrix Machina with Para Kooleo to unlock Darkana VIII - Edge of the Earth
  • Buy the Survarocchi at the top of The Lycaeum to unlock them for any character
  • Buy the Green Eyes Vizard at the top of The Lycaeum to be able to find Bat Dragons in other stages
  • Defeat any Bat Dragon (Currently available in Mad Forest and Il Molise) to unlock the Unearthly Bolt wea;on
  • Evolve the Unearthly Bolt with a maxed Tirajisú to unlock Big Troubler
  • Defeat any Bat Dragon with Big Troubler and Arcana 0 - Game Killer to unlock Darkana 0 - Stake to your Heart
  • Survive 15 minutes in Inverse Boss Rash with Random Events and Random Level Ups to unlock Darkana XIX - Heir of Fate
  • Defeat 2 unique Bat Dragons to unlock a new set of Survarots to purchase from Big Troubler

Detailed info

New stage: The Lycaeum An underwater-themed stage where you press some buttons, beat some crabs, run to the center, kill more things, press more buttons, don’t die. The Drowner can only be defeated via raw damage or by reaching the top of the stage. Hidden treasures can be collected only using Mad Groove or Lavatrix Machina. Teleporters become active after reaching the top once. New character: Para Kooleo Starts with a Move Speed and Duration bonus. When his HP drops below a certain threshold it triggers a Vacuum. He also likes to evolve weapons. He has an abundance of skins. New character: Big Troubler Loves gold and gets trigger happy when he gets gold. The gold also loves him and will protect him at all costs. New weapon: Penshin Fatcha & Tonno Subito / Tonnado / Tonn’omoto / Tonn’oddeeo / Tonne / Unsurpassed / Miracle of Multiplication. Starting weapon for Para Kooleo. Select one of six tuna forms. Evolve it from one to another, stacking stats as you go. Evolve at least once to transform all the Vacuums pickup into "Lavatrix Machina". Then, if you choose to, evolve into the secret evolution, Miracle of Multiplication where everything happens at once. Does not require any items to evolve, but many, many treasure chests. New weapon: Unearthly Bolt & Spirit Disturbance Starting weapon of Big Troubler. Spawns green bolts that attack the closest enemy. It deals increasingly high damage if it Crits in rapid succession. The cap for this damage bonus is determined by Revivals. Evolve with a maxed out Tirajisú. The evolution spawns a green dragon that always deals critical hits. New relic: Green Eyes Vizard Bat Dragons will appear on the Stage Selection menu until they have been defeated at least once. They will appear on the map during a run, and they have to be activated by getting hit. Once active, time stops and enemy waves are changed until they are killed. You can fight them again in new runs, they simply won't be signaled in Stage Selection anymore after getting killed once. New Darkanas: 0 - Stake to your Heart Unlocked by defeating a Bat Dragon with Big Troubler while using the Game Killer Arcana. You will no longer be able to level up using experience gems. Instead, when defeating an enemy, they will also drop a Gold Coin, that you’ll be able to spend at a special merchant to buy weapons. Gold coins will also become your health: don't reach 0 (and quit before Red Death deals the usual 65535 damage per hit to you) New Darkanas: VIII - Edge of the Earth Unlocked by triggering a Lavatrix Machina with Para Kooleo. Gain Thorns and Move Speed locked at 200%, ignore walls, destroy light sources upon contact, and attract things that normally aren’t attracted by a Magnet, like treasure chests. New Darkanas: XIX - Heir of Fate Unlocked by surviving 15 minutes in inverse Boss Rash with Random Events and Random Level Ups enabled. While active, defeating enemies with Fire damage causes them to drop Scorched Souls. Additionally, a Nduja Fritta Tanto will trigger when the character's Health dips to a certain point. New Relics: Survarocchi Unlocked by purchasing it from the Big Troubler merchant in The Lycaeum. Allows Survarot cards to spawn from light sources. Previously available only via the Ante Chamber dlc and a secret character, Survarots Enemahs (Secret rather than Unlockable) Unlocked by purchasing it from the Big Troubler merchant in The Lycaeum after defeating any two unique Bat Dragons. Adds an extra 18 cards based on various enemies to drafts of Survarot. For the full list of bugfixes, please see here: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1794680/view/693137145499484509

1.15 FAQs

How much is 1.15? It’s a free update. Can I now share DLCs when playing online? Not yet, in this patch we managed to do the groundwork to allow for DLC sharing, but we still have to complete the feature. Can I now use Cross-save on PS and Apple+? Not yet. We still don’t have the right policies in place to do that. What platforms is update 1.15 available on? Update 1.15 is launching on Steam first. Other platforms are planned to follow by the end of the month, including Xbox, PlayStation 4/5, Nintendo Switch, Android, iOS, and Epic Games Store. Is update 1.15 coming to Nintendo Switch 2? Yes! Update 1.15 will bring Vampire Survivors to Nintendo Switch 2 for the first time. It won’t arrive at the exact same time as the other platforms, but the current plan is for Nintendo Switch 2 support to follow around two weeks after update 1.15 (but don’t hold us to that). Where are the new achievements? We will sort out the new Steam achievements in the next patch (they will pop automatically). Hey are you still updating Vampire Crawlers? Yes of course, it’s taking longer than expected to release the first QOL improvements patch and a cute looking roadmap because we got stuck for days trying to exit the game.
